subproblem.title: M-absolutely convergent integer series of integer multiplicity currents (Simon 3.13)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T_r ∈ D_n(U) (r ∈ ℕ) integer multiplicity currents and c_r ∈ ℤ such that Σ_r |c_r| M_W(T_r) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U. Then there is S ∈ D_n(U) such that for every ω ∈ D^n(U) the series Σ_r c_r T_r(ω) has (unconditional) sum S(ω), M_W(S) ≤ Σ_r |c_r| M_W(T_r) for every set W ⊆ ℝ^P, and S is integer multiplicity.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ (T : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U n) (c : ℕ → ℤ), (∀ r, IsIntegerMultiplicity (T r)) → (∀ W, CompactlyContainedOpen W U → (∑' r, ((c r).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) * (T r).massOn W) < ∞) → ∃ S : GeometricCurrentOn U n, (∀ ω, HasSum (fun r => (c r : ℝ) * T r ω) (S ω)) ∧ (∀ W, S.massOn W ≤ ∑' r, ((c r).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) * (T r).massOn W) ∧ IsIntegerMultiplicity S
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 3.13 and its printed proof: the integer multiplicity currents are complete for the seminorms M_W; the multiplicities converge in L¹_loc(H^n) to an integer-valued function, the orientations converge, and “T_xM_C = T_xM_Q except for a set of small measure”. Here it is specialised to M-absolutely convergent integer series, which is how 3.13 is used for R^(ℓ), S^(ℓ) in the proof of 7.2; it contains Remark 3.2(1) (sibling im_lincomb). The tangent-space step is supplied by the sibling tangent_locality, and the identity M_W(τ(M,θ,ξ)) = ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n (3.2(3)) by the sibling im_mass_formula.

Notation. H := μHE[n]; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α, a Euclidean norm on Λ^n; ‖ω‖ := sup_x |ω(x)| for a test form ω. For an open set W, W ⊂⊂ U means CompactlyContainedOpen W U.

(CB) (Cauchy–Binet bound; self-contained.) Let τ = (τ₁,…,τ_n) be orthonormal in ℝ^P and ζ := ±simpleNVector τ, so ζ(α) = ±α(τ₁,…,τ_n). Let A_{jk} := ⟨τ_j, e_k⟩ and, for strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin P, let A_I be the n×n minor of A on the columns I. Let dx^I ∈ Λ^n be the covector with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ} for increasing J, so α = Σ_I α(e_I) dx^I.
   (a) For every α ∈ Λ^n, α(τ) = Σ_I α(e_I) det A_I. Expand τ_j = Σ_k A_{jk} e_k by multilinearity; terms with a repeated basis vector vanish by alternation; group the remaining terms by their increasing rearrangement I, the sign of the sorting permutation producing det A_I.
   (b) Σ_I (det A_I)² = 1. Apply (a) to the alternating form α₀(v₁,…,v_n) := det(⟨τ_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} (the wedge of the functionals ⟨τ_i, ·⟩), for which α₀(e_I) = det A_I and α₀(τ) = det(⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) = 1.
   Consequences: by Cauchy–Schwarz in the coordinates (α(e_I))_I, |ζ(α)| ≤ |α| for every α ∈ Λ^n. The covector α^ζ := Σ_I ζ(dx^I) dx^I depends linearly on ζ and satisfies ζ(dx^I) = ±det A_I; hence |α^ζ| = 1 and ζ(α^ζ) = Σ_I (det A_I)² = 1. For n = 0 these claims are immediate (ζ(α) = ±α(), |α| = |α()|). For n > P there is no orthonormal n-frame.

1. (Mass bound.) For X ∈ D_k(U), any set V and η ∈ D^k(U) with tsupport η ⊆ V: ofReal |X(η)| ≤ M_V(X) · ofReal ‖η‖. If ‖η‖ = 0 then η = 0, since |·| is a norm. Otherwise ±η/‖η‖ is admissible for M_V(X), and GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn applies.

2. (Definition of S.) Let ω ∈ D^n(U). Choose an open W ⊂⊂ U with tsupport ω ⊆ W, e.g. W := thickening(δ, tsupport ω) with cthickening(2δ, tsupport ω) ⊆ U. By step 1, Σ_r |c_r T_r(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖ · Σ_r |c_r| M_W(T_r) < ∞; terms with c_r = 0 vanish, and if c_r ≠ 0 then M_W(T_r) < ∞. So (c_r T_r(ω))_r is absolutely summable in ℝ. Let S(ω) be its sum, so HasSum (fun r => c_r T_r(ω)) (S(ω)).

3. (S is a current.) S is linear, by HasSum.add, HasSum.mul_left and linearity of each T_r. For continuity, let ω_q → 0 in D^n(U) (TestFormOnConverges ω_q 0): all tsupport ω_q lie in one compact K ⊆ U, and all derivatives converge uniformly to 0 on K. Choose an open W ⊂⊂ U with K ⊆ W. Then |S(ω_q)| ≤ Σ_r |c_r| |T_r(ω_q)| ≤ ‖ω_q‖ · Σ_r |c_r| M_W(T_r) → 0. Here ‖ω_q‖ → 0 because ω_q → 0 uniformly on K, ω_q = 0 off K, and |·| is bounded by a constant times the operator norm on the finite-dimensional space Λ^n. Hence S is a GeometricCurrentOn U n.

4. (Mass bound for S.) Let V be any set and ω admissible for M_V(S) (tsupport ω ⊆ V, |ω| ≤ 1). By absolute summability and step 1 with ‖ω‖ ≤ 1, ofReal(S(ω)) ≤ Σ_r ofReal(|c_r| |T_r(ω)|) ≤ Σ_r |c_r| M_V(T_r). Taking the supremum gives M_V(S) ≤ Σ'_r |c_r| M_V(T_r).

5. (Representations; finiteness of overlaps.) Let I := {r : c_r ≠ 0}; indices outside I contribute nothing to S. For r ∈ I write T_r = τ(M_r, θ_r, ξ_r) with IsRectifiableTriple U n M_r θ_r ξ_r and θ_r(x) ∈ ℕ for x ∈ M_r; hence θ_r ≥ 1 on M_r. By the sibling im_mass_formula, M_W(T_r) = ∫_{M_r∩W} θ_r dH for open W. So for every W ⊂⊂ U:
   Σ_{r∈I} |c_r| ∫_{M_r∩W} θ_r dH < ∞.   (*)
   Let Θ := Σ_{r∈I} |c_r| θ_r 1_{M_r} : ℝ^P → [0, ∞]. By (*) and monotone convergence, Θ is H-integrable on every W ⊂⊂ U. Since U is a countable union of such W, N_∞ := {x ∈ U : Θ(x) = ∞} is H-null. A point x ∉ N_∞ lies in only finitely many M_r, r ∈ I, because each such r contributes |c_r| θ_r(x) ≥ 1 to Θ(x).

6. (Common tangent planes and orientations.)
   - For r ∈ I the orientation condition gives an H-null set N_r such that for x ∈ M_r ∖ N_r there is an orthonormal τ^r(x) with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M_r θ_r x (span τ^r(x)) and ξ_r(x) = ±simpleNVector τ^r(x).
   - For r, r' ∈ I apply the sibling tangent_locality to (M₁, θ₁) := (M_r, θ_r) and (M₂, θ₂) := (M_{r'}, θ_{r'}); its hypotheses are part of the triple conditions. This gives an H-null set N_{r,r'} such that for x ∈ (M_r ∩ M_{r'}) ∖ N_{r,r'}, every weighted approximate tangent space of (M_r, θ_r) at x is also one of (M_{r'}, θ_{r'}) at x.
   - For x ∈ (M_r ∩ M_{r'}) ∖ (N_r ∪ N_{r'} ∪ N_{r,r'}), both span τ^r(x) and span τ^{r'}(x) are weighted approximate tangent spaces of (M_{r'}, θ_{r'}) at x. They coincide by HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique, as θ_{r'}(x) ≠ 0.
   - Two orthonormal frames of the same n-dimensional subspace differ by an orthogonal matrix O, and simpleNVector(τ O) = det(O) · simpleNVector(τ) with det O = ±1 (multilinearity and alternation). Hence ξ_r(x) = ±ξ_{r'}(x).
   Let N₀ := N_∞ ∪ ⋃_r N_r ∪ ⋃_{r,r'} N_{r,r'}, an H-null set.

7. (Combined multiplicity and orientation.) Let M_∪ := ⋃_{r∈I} M_r. For x ∈ M_∪ ∖ N₀ let r(x) := min{r ∈ I : x ∈ M_r} and ξ̂(x) := ξ_{r(x)}(x). By step 6, for every r ∈ I with x ∈ M_r there is σ_r(x) ∈ {−1, 1} with ξ_r(x) = σ_r(x) ξ̂(x). Explicitly σ_r(x) = ξ_r(x)(β̂(x)), where β̂(x) := α^{ξ̂(x)} is the unit covector dual to ξ̂(x) given by (CB); so σ_r is a.e.-measurable. Define the integer θ̂(x) := Σ_{r∈I} c_r σ_r(x) θ_r(x) 1_{M_r}(x), a finite sum by step 5, and
   M_S := {x ∈ M_∪ ∖ N₀ : θ̂(x) ≠ 0},  θ_S := |θ̂| on M_S (0 elsewhere),  ξ_S := sign(θ̂) ξ̂ on M_S (0 elsewhere).
   No modification is made: these objects are defined pointwise. Off N_∞, θ̂ is a pointwise finite sum of countably many H-a.e.-measurable terms, so θ̂ is H⌞M_∪-a.e. measurable. Hence M_S is H-null-measurable, and θ_S, ξ_S are H⌞M_S-a.e. strongly measurable; r(x) and the indicators 1_{M_r} are built from countably many null-measurable sets.

8. (S = τ(M_S, θ_S, ξ_S).) Let ω ∈ D^n(U) and W ⊂⊂ U open with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Since |ξ_r(x)(α)| ≤ |α| a.e. on M_r by (CB),
Σ_{r∈I} ∫ |c_r θ_r 1_{M_r} ξ_r(ω)| dH ≤ ‖ω‖ Σ_r |c_r| ∫_{M_r∩W} θ_r dH < ∞.
So the series may be integrated term by term (integral_tsum, or dominated convergence for the partial sums):
S(ω) = Σ_r c_r ∫_{M_r} θ_r ξ_r(ω) dH = ∫ Σ_r c_r θ_r 1_{M_r} ξ_r(ω) dH = ∫_{M_∪∖N₀} θ̂ ξ̂(ω) dH = ∫_{M_S} θ_S ξ_S(ω) dH = tauAction n M_S θ_S ξ_S ω.

9. (Triple conditions; S is integer multiplicity.)
   (i) M_S ⊆ M_∪ ⊆ U.
   (ii) M_S is H-null-measurable (step 7).
   (iii) Countable rectifiability: M_r ⊆ M_{r,0} ∪ ⋃_j F_{r,j}(ℝ^n) with H(M_{r,0}) = 0 and F_{r,j} Lipschitz. Hence M_S ⊆ (⋃_r M_{r,0}) ∪ ⋃_{(r,j)} F_{r,j}(ℝ^n), a countable family after reindexing ℕ × ℕ ≃ ℕ, with H-null exceptional set.
   (iv) θ_S(x) = |θ̂(x)| is a positive natural number for x ∈ M_S.
   (v) θ_S ≤ Θ, so θ_S is integrable on M_S ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U: cover K by an open W ⊂⊂ U and use (*).
   (vi) ξ_S is H⌞M_S-a.e. strongly measurable (step 7).
   (vii) Orientation: for each r ∈ I apply tangent_locality to (M₁, θ₁) := (M_r, θ_r) and (M₂, θ₂) := (M_S, θ_S); its hypotheses are the triple conditions of T_r together with (i), (ii), (iv), (v). This gives H-null sets N'_r. Let x ∈ M_S ∖ ⋃_r N'_r and r := r(x). Then x ∈ M_r ∖ N_r, so (M_r, θ_r) has weighted approximate tangent space span τ^r(x) at x, and hence so does (M_S, θ_S). Also ξ_S(x) = ±ξ̂(x) = ±ξ_r(x) = ±simpleNVector τ^r(x).
   Therefore IsRectifiableTriple U n M_S θ_S ξ_S holds, θ_S is natural-valued on M_S, and S(ω) = tauAction n M_S θ_S ξ_S ω for all ω (step 8). So S is integer multiplicity. Together with steps 2–4 this proves the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: Mass bound ⇒ Σ_r c_r T_r(ω) converges absolutely; S is linear and sequentially continuous, and M_W(S) ≤ Σ_r |c_r| M_W(T_r) for every W.
Mass formula ⇒ Σ_r |c_r| ∫_{M_r∩W} θ_r dH^n < ∞; as θ_r ≥ 1, a.e. point lies in only finitely many M_r.
tangent_locality and uniqueness of weighted tangent spaces ⇒ common tangent planes and ξ_r = ±ξ̂ a.e. on overlaps.
θ̂ := Σ_r c_r σ_r θ_r is integer-valued and S = τ({θ̂ ≠ 0}, |θ̂|, sign(θ̂)ξ̂) by termwise integration.
Rectifiable-triple conditions for the new triple; orientation via tangent_locality applied to (M_r, θ_r) and (M_S, θ_S).

audit.reason: The statement correctly specifies unconditional evaluation sums and mass bounds for arbitrary sets. Local absolute summability proves current continuity. Positive integer multiplicities make overlaps finite almost everywhere; tangent locality and uniqueness align orientations, yielding the explicitly constructed integer-valued representation. No reliance on im_lincomb or the parent theorem is needed.
